content:
You can stream with a laptop and webcam, or connect external cameras and audio equipment through an encoder. Before you use either setup for a service, test the picture, sound, and connection together.

This guide uses YouTube Live and OBS Studio as a worked example. For permissions, use [Copyright Licenses for Worship and Streaming](/wiki/administrative/legal/copyright-licenses-for-worship-and-streaming).

---

## Trace the signal path

An encoder prepares video for the streaming platform. You can run encoding software on a computer or use a standalone hardware encoder.

For a computer setup, identify the parts below. OBS supports camera capture, audio inputs, and images or text within scenes.

| Your setup | Select in your setup |
|---|---|
| Video | Webcam, or camera through a compatible capture device |
| Sound | The intended microphone or audio input |
| Scene | OBS scenes containing the sources you want to show |
| Feed | The YouTube stream URL and stream key in your encoder |

In OBS, add the picture through the Sources dock. Select the intended audio device in Settings, then check that its meter responds when you speak.

---

## Check the camera connection

A webcam and an HDMI camera take different connection paths. For example, Elgato's Cam Link setup connects a camera's HDMI output to the capture device, then connects that device to the computer by USB.

For that kind of camera setup, check the manufacturer's instructions for removing battery icons and other display information from the HDMI picture. Elgato calls this clean HDMI output. Also check automatic shutoff and the camera's supported continuous-power arrangement. Elgato's camera tips are general guidance, so confirm what applies to your model.

In OBS's Video Capture Device properties, choose the actual capture device. On Windows, an unsupported resolution or frame rate can leave the source blank. Check supported modes before forcing a custom setting.

---

## Build an online audio mix

Listen to the mix intended for the stream. Yamaha's church audio guide explains that copying the room mix can leave online listeners with a thin, vocal-heavy sound because they do not hear the room's acoustic contribution.

Where your mixer supports it, consider a separate mix for online listeners. An auxiliary bus is one option. A pre-fader auxiliary mix allows adjustments there without changing the main mix. Follow your console's manual for its routing controls.

In OBS, avoid capturing the same audio device both globally and as a scene audio source. OBS warns that this can create echo. If you add the device directly to scenes, disable its global capture first.

<Callout type="tip">
Record a rehearsal and listen back before going live. OBS recommends checking sound at the device and again in OBS, then listening to a recorded session before the broadcast.
</Callout>

---

## Configure the encoder

Run OBS's Auto-Configuration Wizard as a starting point. It considers your computer and network conditions. Then review the output settings against your platform's current guidance.

For YouTube, set resolution, frame rate, and bitrate in the encoder. Its bitrate recommendations depend on the codec as well as the resolution and frame rate. Choose a quality your connection can deliver reliably.

| YouTube setting | Current guidance |
|---|---|
| Connection protocol | YouTube recommends RTMPS |
| Bitrate encoding | CBR |
| Keyframe interval | Recommended 2 seconds; do not exceed 4 seconds |

<Callout type="important">
Platform guidance was checked October 16, 2026. Before configuring a stream, confirm current encoder settings, bitrate recommendations, eligibility, and controls with YouTube Help. Check OBS and your equipment manufacturer's documentation for your installed software and hardware.
</Callout>

---

## Test the upload connection

Measure upload speed at the streaming location. Download speed can be higher than upload speed, and other people sharing the network can reduce the bandwidth available to you. YouTube recommends leaving room beyond the total streaming bitrate.

OBS recommends a wired connection because Wi-Fi may be unstable for streaming. Use a wired connection for the test where available, then send a test stream through the platform.

If OBS reports dropped frames from the connection, check network stability and whether the configured bitrate exceeds what the connection can sustain. Lowering video bitrate is one troubleshooting step OBS recommends.

---

## Rehearse before the public stream

Check your channel's live-streaming eligibility and enable the feature before rehearsal. Create a test stream with its visibility deliberately set to private.

- [ ] Confirm the intended camera and audio devices in OBS.
- [ ] Include speech, music, and movement representative of the service in the test.
- [ ] Listen to the recording for distortion and check the sound at its source.
- [ ] Check playback on a phone and verify the event's watch page.
- [ ] Review stream-health messages in YouTube's Live Control Room.

<Callout type="warning">
Check auto-start before sending an encoder feed. When enabled, it lets you start the stream from the encoder. YouTube's Reuse settings also copies auto-start and auto-stop selections.
</Callout>

---

## Run and end the stream

For a scheduled YouTube stream with auto-start off, start the encoder and wait for the preview in Live Control Room. Check the preview before choosing Go live.

Continue checking audio and video quality during the event. Use the watch page as well as the encoder's own picture and sound checks.

To finish the scheduled stream, choose End Stream in Live Control Room and stop sending content from the encoder. If you made a local recording, verify the file rather than assuming the recording succeeded.

Treat the stream key as a password. If it is compromised, a channel owner or manager can reset it in Live Control Room and update the encoder with the replacement.

---

## Find the failing link

Use the symptom to decide where to look first.

| Symptom | First check |
|---|---|
| Blank camera source | Selected capture device and supported resolution or frame rate |
| No input-meter movement | The audio device selected in OBS |
| Echo | The same audio device captured globally and in a scene |
| Bad picture or sound inside the encoder | Source quality and the local recording |
| Healthy encoder, poor online playback | Outbound connection and stream-health messages |

If only one viewer reports trouble, YouTube suggests checking that viewer's device or connection. If viewers on different connections report the same problem, investigate the encoder and outgoing stream.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"But all things must be done properly and in an orderly manner."* — 1 Corinthians 14:40 (LSB)
</Callout>

title: Streaming Equipment and Setup

sources.claim: Opening and signal path: YouTube supports webcam and encoder approaches; an encoder prepares video, runs on a computer or standalone hardware, and accepts external audio/video. Trace destination and scheduled-stream operation: enter stream URL/key, start encoder, inspect preview, Go live, then End Stream and stop encoder.
sources.quote: converts your video into a digital format to stream on YouTube.

sources.claim: Run and end: scheduled stream preview comes before Go live. Starting/stopping the encoder and ending the stream follow the scheduled workflow, with auto-start addressed separately.
sources.quote: wait for the stream preview to show up, and then click Go live.

sources.claim: Opening, signal path, audio device selection, wizard, rehearsal and missing-audio troubleshooting: OBS scenes contain sources; select hardware via Sources/Settings; watch input meters; wizard considers computer resources and network conditions; test before first stream.
sources.quote: your computer's hardware resources, and your network conditions

sources.claim: Signal path and camera: OBS accepts webcams and capture cards as Video Capture Device sources; select the device in properties. Windows custom resolution/frame rate must be supported or nothing displays, also supporting the blank-source troubleshooting row.
sources.quote: If the device does not support the resolution, the source will not display anything

sources.claim: Signal path and camera: selection of the capture device in source properties.
sources.quote: select your device from the Device drop down list.

sources.claim: Camera connection: Elgato Cam Link guide pp.2-3 shows HDMI camera to capture device to USB computer; clean HDMI removes camera interface information. Check model instructions for shutoff and continuous power; the tips may not apply to every model.

sources.quote: connect your camera to the HDMI input

sources.publisher: Elgato, Getting Started with Cam Link 4K

sources.claim: Online audio pp.4-5: the house mix may be thin/vocal-heavy online because of acoustic differences; a separate stream mix can use an auxiliary bus, and pre-fader aux adjustments do not change the mains; console routing follows its manual.
sources.publisher: Yamaha, Doug Gould, Improve the Sound on Your Livestreams
sources.quote: people listening online don’t hear the ambient sounds.

sources.claim: Online audio p.5: distinct online mix; an auxiliary bus is an option, and its pre-fader settings support independent adjustments.
sources.publisher: Yamaha, Doug Gould, Improve the Sound on Your Livestreams
sources.quote: create a separate mix for your remote audience.

sources.claim: Online audio p.5: pre-fader aux level changes do not affect the main mix.
sources.publisher: Yamaha, Doug Gould, Improve the Sound on Your Livestreams
sources.quote: it will not affect the mains.

sources.claim: Online audio and echo troubleshooting: avoid duplicate global/scene capture of one device; disable global capture first if adding scene devices.
sources.quote: Audio Input/Output Capture source can cause an echo effect if you have the same device selected in Settings -> Audio.

sources.claim: Audio tip, rehearsal, levels: listen at source and in OBS, then record and listen back before public streaming; distortion is a signal-level issue to check at the device.
sources.quote: Always start at the device in question.

sources.claim: Audio tip and rehearsal checklist: listen back to a normal recorded session before streaming.
sources.quote: record a session as you normally would and then listen back to the file before going live.

sources.claim: Encoder: set resolution/frame rate/bitrate in encoder; recommendations vary by codec and video format; reliable quality depends on upload. claim_check.notes: Passed at reviewed draft commit a9b115c4722bfdae74c8430757c897895138d10b. The 9ce7c6f review (PR #38 comment 6206320754) passed every source claim except B1. a9b115c removes only the unsupported speed-test sentence and the matching phrase in the OBS Stream Connection Troubleshooting source claim; the remaining paragraph matches that page (wired connection recommended because Wi-Fi may be unstable; dropped frames mean an unstable connection or an unsustainable bitrate; lower the video bitrate). 1 Corinthians 14:40 (LSB) matched word for word in the prior review and is unchanged. bin/wiki lint passes (1,037 words, no warnings). Desktop 1280 and mobile 390 screenshots show complete content, readable tables and checklist, and the LSB notice. This is editorial content/tooling proof, not application acceptance.

rulings: Use YouTube Live and OBS as an explicit worked example; do not imply that all platforms share controls or eligibility.
Technical operation only. Streaming strategy remains B6; licensing is delegated to the published copyright article without restating rules.
Do not prescribe prices, camera counts, universal upload speeds, audio level targets or a church purchasing timeline. Current platform recommendations are dated 2026-10-16.
Use model-dependent camera power/shutoff guidance, rather than assuming that all cameras can run from USB power or expose the same HDMI settings.
